conventions.convention: The age model has unit characteristic speed, bounded nonnegative Lipschitz mortality and fertility, nonnegative L1 initial density, and renewal inflow B(t)=∫β(a)n(t,a) da. Survival is S(a,s)=exp(-∫ from a to a+s of μ).
The finite-age model assumes 0<T<A and removes cohorts upon reaching A. Consequently no newborn cohort reaches the outflow boundary during the stated horizon.

The size interval is fixed, growth is bounded Lipschitz and strictly positive, γ is parent removal, and K_y itself records daughter production. K_y may be atomic and is supported on [0,y]; daughter production is not additionally multiplied by γ in the equation.
Size cells are disjoint, with the final cell including X. The discrete size moment weights cell masses by cell centers; it is distinct from an exact continuous first moment.

Birth quadrature acts on fertility within each cell and multiplies its estimate by the cell density. Adaptive acceptance controls an indicator only; convergence requires a separate true quadrature-defect bound.
The age finite-volume grid has Δt=T/N and Δa=A/J, uses fixed quadrature settings over time, and requires Δt/Δa+Δt‖μ‖∞≤1. Births enter through F_0, while F_J is discarded as absorbing outflow.

Cohort levels stop at N=floor(T/Δt). Existing cohorts advance before a newborn mass Δt B_h^k is inserted at age zero at t_(k+1). Consistency is measured in BL*, using ‖φ‖∞+Lip(φ)≤1, rather than L1 distance between atoms and densities.

Smooth finite-volume convergence assumes a C2 solution on the closed time-age rectangle, including renewal-corner compatibility. BV convergence assumes no such compatibility and uses cutoffs tending to infinity and a positive two-sided mesh-ratio bound.

load_bearing.statement: There is a unique mild solution. Its birth rate is the unique continuous solution of B(t)=G(t)+∫₀ᵗK(a)B(t-a) da, and its density is n₀(a-t)S(a-t,t) for a≥t and B(t-a)S(0,a) for a<t.

Positive birth quadrature satisfies 0≤B_h≤β∞Σ_jM_j. Under the stated CFL, nonnegative initial masses remain nonnegative, N_h^(k+1)≤(1+Δt β∞)N_h^k, and two runs with the same grid, rates and quadrature rule satisfy ‖M^(k+1)-M̃^(k+1)‖₁≤(1+Δt β∞)‖M^k-M̃^k‖₁.

For the finite-age model, the displayed Volterra equation has a unique continuous nonnegative birth rate and determines the unique mild solution. Its mass is at most exp(β∞t)‖n₀ᴬ‖₁, and for t≤T<A its cumulative outflow is ∫ from A-t to A of n₀ᴬ(x)S(x,A-x) dx.

The solution map is linear and positive, with ‖S_(μ,β)(t)n₀‖₁≤exp(β∞t)‖n₀‖₁. For the two stated models, with δ=‖μ-μ̃‖∞+‖β-β̃‖∞, the data-and-coefficient difference is at most exp(β∞t)(‖n₀-ñ₀‖₁+δt exp(β̃∞t)‖ñ₀‖₁).

Under the stated compatible C2 finite-age solution, exact initial cell masses, positive two-sided mesh-ratio bounds and CFL, max_k E_k≤C_T(Δa+Δt+ε_Q), with the same reconstructed L1 order. Midpoint quadrature gives ε_Q≤C_TΔa; adaptive indicators do not replace a true ε_Q bound.

The extended size IVP has a unique strictly increasing characteristic on [0,T]. Under the size-scheme CFL, masses remain nonnegative and satisfy the displayed exact number and center-weighted-size balances; division preserves the discrete size moment only when daughter first-moment production cancels parent removal.

For A>T, cumulative initial-cohort outflow is bounded by ∫ from A-T to infinity of n₀, and sup_(0≤t≤T)‖n(t)-nᴬ(t)‖₁≤2exp(β∞T)∫ from A-T to infinity of n₀. Under the smooth discretization hypotheses, add C_T(Δa+Δt+ε_Q) for the fully discrete error.

published_dependencies.used_for: The differentiable IVP convention underlying age and size characteristics.
Infinite-age mass and coefficient/data stability bounds, and the finite-age mass bound; the forcing functions used are constant or explicitly nondecreasing.
Uniform short-time existence and uniqueness for the bounded globally Lipschitz extension of the size growth field, followed by finite continuation.

seams_checked.note: Read the one-step definition and Euler theorem. The cohort proof constructs a C1 mortality extension, an open domain with convex state fibers, and a compact survival tube. Its local defect convention and stability use match the supplier.

Read the midpoint algorithm, panel-kernel lemma and composite error theorem. One-panel parent/cell formulas preserve positive weights and admissible intervals; the smooth convergence proof applies the C2 error estimate to smooth integrands.

Read the finite geometric recurrence lemma. Cohort survival uses the aligned horizon T_h=NΔt; smooth midpoint convergence obtains O(Δt²) forcing using the mesh-ratio bound. No log-density conclusion is imported.

Read the capped algorithm, indicator definition, Simpson formula and termination/budget proof. Birth quadrature retains failure/cap statuses and positive leaf estimates. The page and convergence theorem explicitly separate indicators from true quadrature error.

Read the grid definition and smooth-stencil consistency theorem. The age scheme uses uniform-grid conventions and proves its renewal-boundary, mortality, positivity and convergence claims locally; it does not apply periodic Fourier or smooth-periodic consistency results to the renewal boundary or BV data.
